clue.text: Person penning international correspondence

indicators.note: to pen something is to shut it in an enclosure, so the person word surrounds the other piece

parts.note: a party is a person in the legal sense, as in 'the guilty party'

explanation.surface: Someone is writing letters to people abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Person' reads as a letter-writer, but it is PARTY in its legal sense of one participant in a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: Parity is equality or equivalence between things, which is what correspondence means in a mathematical sense.

clue.text: Dirty election must be oddly disregarded

parts.note: a poll is a vote or election

indicators.note: ignoring the odd-numbered letters leaves only the even ones of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A grubby election should be ignored as an odd affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly disregarded' drops letters 1, 3 and 5 of 'must be', keeping UTE.
explanation.definitionFit: To pollute is to contaminate, a synonym of dirty used as a verb.

clue.text: Bruiser arranged with me to pay back cash

indicators.note: letters arranged anew are put in a different order, so the two words are rearranged together

explanation.surface: A heavy has been lined up with the speaker to return some money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges BRUISER plus ME.
explanation.definitionFit: To reimburse is to repay money someone has spent or lost.

clue.text: The head of this old English newspaper is a slimeball

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, taken from the next word

parts.note: rag is slang for a low-quality newspaper

explanation.surface: The editor of a tabloid is described as a nasty piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: A toerag is British slang for a contemptible person.
explanation.definitionFit: Toerag and slimeball are both slang insults for a despicable, untrustworthy person.

clue.text: Angry rap music mainly revolving around money, essentially

indicators.note: around tells us the shuffled letters sit on either side of the next piece
revolving suggests letters turning about into a new order
mainly means most of the word, so its last letter is dropped
the essence of a word is its central letter

explanation.surface: Rap songs mostly circling around cash make someone cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' drops the last letter of 'music'; 'revolving' shuffles the result with 'rap', and 'around' wraps that jumble round N, the centre of 'money' from 'essentially'.
explanation.definitionFit: Up in arms is an idiom for being indignant and protesting, a state of anger.

clue.text: Look, hold up!

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters read from the bottom to the top

parts.note: to keep something is to retain it

explanation.surface: Someone says 'Look, wait!' to stop another person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold up' reads as 'wait', but 'up' turns KEEP backwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A peek is a quick glance, so it is a kind of look.

clue.text: Marines manoeuvring south narrowly avoided collision

indicators.note: manoeuvring moves things around, so the letters of the word are reordered

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Marines moving south only just escape a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvring' looks like a military verb but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A near miss is an incident where two vehicles almost hit one another.

clue.text: Portuguese king ultimately letting queen be in command

parts.note: rei is the Portuguese word for king

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A monarch in Lisbon finally allows his queen to take charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes the last letters of 'letting queen', G and N.
explanation.definitionFit: To reign is to rule as a monarch, holding supreme command.

clue.text: Comes forward for flight in an excited state

parts.note: a flight of stairs is a set of steps
up can mean stirred up or excited, as in 'all het up'

explanation.surface: Someone eagerly moves ahead to board a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' suggests air travel; it is a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: To step up is to volunteer or present oneself, which is coming forward.

clue.text: Hang about in a Brummie's barge?

indicators.note: a Brummie is someone from Birmingham, England, whose accent turns a long 'i' vowel into an 'oi' sound

parts.note: a lighter is a flat-bottomed barge for unloading ships

explanation.surface: A Birmingham boatman asks whether to linger on his barge.
explanation.walkthrough: The Birmingham accent pronounces the long 'i' sound close to 'oi', so LIGHTER, a barge, is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To loiter is to linger idly, which is what hanging about means.

clue.text: Reserve is assigned a team

parts.note: a set task is one assigned to someone
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: A substitute player is allocated to a squad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserve' suggests a substitute player; it is the verb meaning to keep back.
explanation.definitionFit: To set aside is to keep something back for later use, the verb sense of reserve.

clue.text: Support friend without breaking the law!

parts.note: a leg supports a table or a body
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Backing a mate while staying within the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something legally means acting in keeping with statute, so no offence is committed.

clue.text: A rubbish bin used outside is not loaded

indicators.note: outside means one word wraps round the other piece
rubbish as an adjective means poor or messy, telling us the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A garbage can placed out on the street holds nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubbish' looks like the bin's contents but is the anagram signal; 'outside' then wraps the remaining word round the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A loaded question or die is weighted to one side, so something not loaded is impartial.

clue.text: You said it! In the end, demand always changes

parts.note: amen is said to agree emphatically, like 'you said it!'

indicators.note: in the end points to the final letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Agreeing that someone who insists on things will always end up with change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the end' takes D and S from 'demand always'.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend is to alter or revise, so amends means makes changes to.

clue.text: Plane not working at full speed

parts.note: a plane is a flat surface
out can mean switched off or out of action

explanation.surface: An aircraft breaks down while racing at top speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plane' suggests an aircraft; it is the geometric sense, a flat surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat out is an idiom for going as fast as possible, with maximum effort.

clue.text: Bring in bits for repairing on a regular basis

indicators.note: bits of a word are some of its letters, here the ones picked from the next word
regular means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Someone is paid for fixing parts at fixed intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bits for ... on a regular basis' takes letters 2, 4, 6 and 8 of 'repairing'.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn is to receive money as wages, so it brings income in.

clue.text: Sweet topping made from apples cooked with rum and a touch of yoghurt

indicators.note: cooked suggests something altered by preparation, so the letters are mixed
a touch of something is a small amount, here its first letter

explanation.surface: A recipe for a dessert sauce of stewed apples, rum and a dab of yoghurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges APPLES, RUM and Y, the first letter of 'yoghurt', from 'a touch of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Maple syrup is a sugary liquid poured over pancakes and desserts as a topping.

clue.text: Under restraint, police officers toughen up

indicators.note: in a down entry, under puts one piece below the other

parts.note: a rein is a strap that restrains a horse
the force is a collective name for the police

explanation.surface: Officers held back by rules are told to get tougher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under' places FORCE beneath REIN in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinforce is to strengthen, making something tougher or more resistant.

clue.text: Kid endlessly adjusted screen time on the sly

indicators.note: without its ends a word keeps only its middle letter
adjusted means altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A child keeps fiddling with the screen-time settings without anyone knowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' leaves I from KID; 'adjusted' rearranges SCREEN to NSECRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in secret means doing it furtively or slyly, out of view.

clue.text: New record tends to be welcomed by clubs after hours

indicators.note: to be welcomed by is to be taken in, so the pieces around it hold this one

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
late means after the usual time
to tend towards is to lean, an inclination

explanation.surface: A new music release is taken up by nightclubs in the small hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record' looks musical, but a record here is a history, as in criminal record.
explanation.definitionFit: A clean slate is a fresh start with past wrongdoing wiped away, a new record.

clue.text: Dictionary publisher's change involving a couple of lines

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: coins are small change
L is the abbreviation for line, so two lines are LL

explanation.surface: A dictionary maker revises its text with a couple of extra lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Collins is a long-established publisher of English and bilingual dictionaries.

clue.text: Video corporation changing hands

indicators.note: hands here are right and left, so one hand's letter is exchanged for the other's

parts.note: a firm is a business corporation

explanation.surface: A video company passes to new owners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing hands' suggests a sale; it swaps R (right) for L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: To video something is to record it on camera, which is to film it.

clue.text: Married individual mostly looked to get rich

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, so its final letter goes

parts.note: one is a single individual
eyed means looked at

explanation.surface: A married person nearly kept watch for wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts ONE to ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Moneyed means having a lot of money, a synonym of wealthy or rich.

clue.text: Audible sign of hesitation in boy's talk

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a son is a boy; the possessive just joins the clue
erm is the noise people make when hesitating

explanation.surface: A lad's speech is full of audible stalling noises.
explanation.definitionFit: A sermon is a talk given by a preacher, often a long moralising one.

clue.text: Oppressive main space

parts.note: the lead is the main item or role, as in 'lead story'
an en is a printing space, half an em wide

explanation.surface: A sense of heavy gloom fills the principal room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' suggests the sea; here it means principal. An en is a typesetting term for a space.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaden means heavy or dull, used of an oppressive atmosphere or sky.

clue.text: NY prosecutor upset with Mafioso's additional charge

indicators.note: upset in a down entry means turned upside down, so read bottom to top

parts.note: DA is a district attorney, the public prosecutor in New York
a don is a Mafia boss

explanation.surface: A New York prosecutor is angered by a gangster's extra criminal charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks emotional but flips DA in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An add-on is an extra item, often sold for an extra fee on top of a base price.

clue.text: Obsessive's fear spun out of control

indicators.note: out of control suggests chaos, so the letters fall into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone's anxiety has spiralled beyond management.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of control' rearranges FEAR and SPUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A superfan is an extremely devoted, fixated enthusiast, an obsessive follower.

clue.text: Reverberating sound of dance music lacking tone, oddly

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the picked letters are removed

parts.note: techno is a style of electronic dance music

indicators.note: oddly picks the first, third and other odd-numbered letters

explanation.surface: A club track that is strangely out of tune echoes around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes T and N from 'tone', and 'lacking' removes them from TECHNO.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is a sound reflected back so that it is heard again.

clue.text: Popular guide for rambling

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
to direct is to guide

explanation.surface: A well-loved guidebook for hill walkers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rambling' suggests countryside walks; it means roundabout or digressive.
explanation.definitionFit: Indirect means roundabout rather than straight, as rambling speech wanders from the point.

clue.text: Bootlicking soldiers following Sergeant Major

indicators.note: following places the soldiers piece after the other

parts.note: an army is a body of soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops creep after their sergeant major.
explanation.definitionFit: Smarmy means ingratiating and obsequious, the manner of a toady or flatterer.

clue.text: A snack regularly being covered in nuts is not OK!

indicators.note: covered in means the outer piece wraps the inner
nuts means crazy, so the letters go wild
regularly picks letters at steady intervals

explanation.surface: Eating a snack coated in nuts is forbidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes A, N, C from 'A snack'; 'nuts' scrambles IS NOT to STION, which 'being covered in' wraps around them.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanction is to approve or authorise, which is what OK means as a verb.

clue.text: Switch company, having no start or end plan

indicators.note: no start or end means the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: Nintendo makes the Switch games console

explanation.surface: Someone means to change employers with no clear plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switch' looks like a verb; it is the Nintendo games console.
explanation.definitionFit: To intend is to have something in mind as an aim, which is to plan it.
